summary: A narrator visits an elderly, sharp-tongued former lawyer to seek help for their brother Wilson, who has been arrested by the FBI along with others accused of terrorism. The narrator argues the case was an entrapment by an informant nicknamed Zip, who got Wilson to like him, while the woman dismisses the idea and asks about Wilson's record. The excerpt also describes the cluttered, filthy house the woman lives in, and ends as she prepares tea in the kitchen.
one_line: A young narrator pleads with a retired lawyer to help their brother, arrested by the FBI in an alleged terror plot involving an informant.
key_facts: The FBI picked Wilson up the morning of the visit, along with a number of other people.
The narrator says one of the arrested group is probably an FBI informant and that the group is accused of being terrorists, which the narrator denies.
The narrator believes the informant, whom the narrator calls Zip, set the group up by finding people naive enough to talk about wanting to do something.
The narrator says Wilson wanted Zip to like him and that Wilson kind of fell under Zip's spell.
The woman says that if Zip works for the FBI he will have been given strict instructions because the FBI knows how to get around an entrapment defense.
The woman remarks that the name Zip is ludicrous.
The woman asks how old the brother is, and the narrator answers twenty-three.
The woman says the brother is old enough to know better and asks whether he has a record.
The narrator says Wilson has never been convicted of anything.
The woman says it was a waste of the narrator's time because she is retired.
The narrator mentions that Asif Ranjha and Xavier Jackson needed the woman's help, and the woman dismisses it as charming.
The house is full of books, papers, piles of unopened mail, yellowed newspapers, rusty hardware, and a filthy carpet.
The kitchen counter is covered with stuff, the floor is sticky, and the stovetop looks as if it has not been wiped in a decade.
The woman's kettle whistles and she leads the narrator inside, moving in a lopsided way as if walking hurts.
